clue.text: United, with excellent scoring shot, back in the perfect place to be

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: back tells us to read the excellent and shot pieces from right to left

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with I for the figure 1
a pot is a scoring shot in snooker or pool

explanation.surface: A sports report: United, after a fine scoring shot, are back where they want to be.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) is written with the letter I for the figure 1; a pot is a snooker scoring shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined ideal society, an idyllic spot where everything is flawless.

clue.text: Time in employment erasing end of idle interval

indicators.note: erasing tells us a letter is wiped out of the time and employment pieces

parts.note: someone in employment has been hired

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word idle

explanation.surface: A worker is taken on just as a spell of idleness comes to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erasing' removes E, the last letter of 'idle', from T + HIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a third is the interval spanning three notes of the scale, such as C up to E.

clue.text: Ideal place is available in March?

indicators.note: available in suggests one thing can be found inside another, so is goes within the march word

parts.note: a parade is a march, a procession

explanation.surface: Asking whether the perfect spot can be had during the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month, but here it is a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is heaven or Eden, the supreme idyllic location.

clue.text: Article promoted in drinks range?

indicators.note: promoted means moved up, which in a down entry means earlier in the word for drinks

parts.note: laps means drinks, as a cat does milk
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper item pushing a line of drinks products.
explanation.walkthrough: In LAPS the A is moved up one place, giving ALPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain chain of central Europe, a range of peaks.

clue.text: Street's bare, with daughter leaving after greeting

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail

indicators.note: leaving says the daughter letter departs from the word for bare

parts.note: nude means bare, unclothed

explanation.surface: A deserted street once the girl has gone, after a hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the greeting first; Ave is Latin for hail.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad road in a town, often lined with trees.

clue.text: Clubs supporting distressed top goalie offering explanations

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece sits beneath the rest
distressed means upset or damaged, so the letters of top goalie are jumbled

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Football clubs back their upset star keeper as he justifies himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' mixes TOP GOALIE into APOLOGETI, and C goes under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apologetic in the old sense means making a defence or justification of something.

clue.text: Praises kinky sex, keeping a large number upset

indicators.note: keeping says the anagram holds another piece inside it
kinky means twisted, so the letters of sex are rearranged
upset in a down entry turns the large-number word upside down, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: a lot is a large number

explanation.surface: Someone lauds unconventional sex, while plenty of people are offended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' gives EXS from the fodder; 'upset' gives TOL, which 'keeping' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, to laud.

clue.text: Describing some bonds slipping in value? Not yielding nothing

indicators.note: slipping suggests the letters of in value slide out of place
yielding means giving up, so the word not surrenders a letter

parts.note: O is the zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A financial question about bonds losing worth and paying no return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipping' turns IN VALUE into UNIVALE; 'yielding' takes O from NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a univalent atom forms a single bond, having a valency of one.

clue.text: Church support overlooking holy man's tweet

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the saint letters are left out of the support word

parts.note: a stirrup supports a rider's foot
ST stands for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A church backing a cleric's message on social media, but ignoring him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tweet' looks like social media; it is birdsong. The support is a rider's foot-rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is a bird's short repeated chirp, which is a tweet.

clue.text: Names rebel at work in towns

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: cities are large towns

indicators.note: at work suggests the letters of rebel are busy being rearranged

explanation.surface: Listing rebels active in various towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' gives ELEBR, which sits just after the first letter of the towns word.
explanation.definitionFit: Big names are famous people, stars of public life.

clue.text: Gets thanks when filling ordinary containers

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the thanks word is put within the containers

parts.note: bins are containers
ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: Someone receives gratitude for stuffing everyday containers.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is a casual British word for 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or receive it.

clue.text: Son looks round that place, finding lots of pieces

indicators.note: round says the looks word goes around the place word

parts.note: miens are looks or expressions
there means that place

explanation.surface: A boy glances around a spot and discovers lots of fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: A mien is a person's look or bearing, an old-fashioned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed to smithereens means broken into countless tiny fragments.

clue.text: Superior American performed in US city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
did means performed, carried out

explanation.surface: A haughty American gave a show in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes someone affectedly posh, putting on airs of being above others.

clue.text: Enhancement for viewers almost crazy to get odd vegetable

parts.note: kohl is eye make-up, enhancing the eyes, which are viewers

indicators.note: almost means the crazy word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: rabid means frenzied or crazy

explanation.surface: Something to sharpen one's eyesight nearly drives someone mad over a peculiar vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' are eyes, enhanced by kohl.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a strange-looking cabbage-family vegetable with a swollen globe stem.

clue.text: Unconnected item in footwear — half a pair? Tip of toe to probe that

indicators.note: to probe means to poke inside, so the toe's tip goes into the footwear pieces

parts.note: a sandal is an item of footwear

indicators.note: tip of picks the first letter of toe

parts.note: one is half of a pair of two

explanation.surface: A lone shoe, missing its partner, with a toe poking into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The toe's tip goes in just after the first letter of the footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-alone device or item works independently, not linked to anything else.

clue.text: Temporary worker at home perhaps resentful about curtailed opening

indicators.note: about says the resentful word goes around the other piece

parts.note: bitter means resentful

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the opening word loses its last letter

parts.note: an abyss is a deep opening or chasm

explanation.surface: An aggrieved temp at home complains about a shortened job start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' trims ABYS from the chasm word; it sits after the first letter of the resentful word.
explanation.definitionFit: A babysitter is someone briefly minding children in their house, short-term domestic help.

clue.text: Large amount of drink — reduced concern — one's driven wildly

parts.note: a bumper is a glass filled to the brim

indicators.note: reduced means the concern word is cut short by a letter

parts.note: care means concern

explanation.surface: Heavy drinking, a dwindling sense of worry, and someone careering about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests drink-driving; 'one's driven wildly' is the fairground car.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper car is a dodgem, steered chaotically into others at a funfair.

clue.text: Network has me next to mum

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A web of family connections puts a person beside their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother; it means keep quiet, SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is a net, an interlaced network of threads.

clue.text: Vessel runs into catastrophe in developing area

indicators.note: into says the vessel and runs pieces go inside the catastrophe word

parts.note: doom is catastrophe or ruin
an ark is a vessel, like Noah's
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A ship hits disaster in an emerging region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' suggests economic growth; here it is film processing.
explanation.definitionFit: A darkroom is the unlit space where photographic film is processed.

clue.text: Item of poetry penned by William Blake

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the letters sit inside the poet's name

explanation.surface: A poem written by the Romantic poet William Blake.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot, an unstressed beat then a stressed one.

clue.text: Lot of material going off with TNT? It would cause explosions

indicators.note: going off means exploding, so the letters are blown into a new order
lot of means most of, so the word material loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Most of a substance detonating with dynamite would cause blasts.
explanation.walkthrough: MATERIA plus TNT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: When antimatter meets ordinary matter both annihilate, releasing huge bursts of energy.

clue.text: Map possible Martian's origin

parts.note: to plan is to map out
ET is the film extraterrestrial, a possible alien visitor

explanation.surface: Charting where an alien might have come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is the fourth world from the Sun, home of any Martian.

clue.text: Island secures contract with Georgia for chemical quantity

indicators.note: secures means holds firmly, so the island word wraps round the others

parts.note: a deal is a contract
GA is the postal code for the US state Georgia

explanation.surface: An island nation signs a trade agreement with Georgia over some chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal gas is a theoretical substance obeying the gas laws exactly, a model used in chemistry.

clue.text: Record endorsements involving Judge back in Balkan capital

indicators.note: back means the whole assembly is read in reverse
involving means including, so the record wraps round the judge letter

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
OKs are approvals or endorsements

explanation.surface: A music release with approval from a judge returns to a city in the Balkans.
explanation.walkthrough: EJP + OKS reads backwards to give the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Skopje is the capital city of North Macedonia, in the Balkan peninsula.

clue.text: Writing in support of case of sabotage

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: case of means the outer letters, the casing, of sabotage

explanation.surface: Writing in favour of a sabotage case.
explanation.definitionFit: Prose is ordinary written language, as opposed to verse.

clue.text: Staff on both sides of a street

indicators.note: on both sides of says the staff word flanks the a, holding it inside

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Employees lined up on each side of a city street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like workers; it is a stick, ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a public way for traffic, much like a street.

clue.text: Contralto's ending, say, in lower part of duet

parts.note: the word contralto contains the letter O twice, and its final letter is the later of the pair; say flags this as a description

explanation.surface: A singer's final note sounding in the bottom line of a duet.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as 'second O' and it describes the last letter of CONTRALTO, which has two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet the secondo is the player taking the bass part.

clue.text: Old party to get excited endlessly, making a stink

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: endlessly means the excited word loses its last letter

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up or excite

explanation.surface: A former political party becomes agitated without end and causes a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a stink' looks like causing trouble; it means smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Odorous means smelly, giving off a strong odour.

clue.text: Legal document getting that chap to squirm

parts.note: a writ is a legal document
he means that chap

explanation.surface: A man served with legal papers is left wriggling.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and wriggle in pain or discomfort.

clue.text: Girl showing staunch character, mostly

parts.note: to staunch a flow is to dam it

indicators.note: mostly means the character word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: self means one's nature or character

explanation.surface: A young woman displaying firm character, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staunch' looks like the adjective 'loyal'; it is the verb, to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A damsel is an old word for a young unmarried woman.
